subject: English
questionText:
Choose the correct one-word substitution for the phrase below:

"An action done by one's own free will, without being forced or paid."
solution:
Voluntary means done, given, or acting of one's own free will.

Other options: • Compulsory / Obligatory: Required by law or a rule; mandatory.
• Involuntary: Done without will or conscious control.
Vocab Meanings: • Voluntary: Done of one's own free will (स्वैच्छिक)
• Compulsory: Required by law or rule (अनिवार्य)
• Obligatory: Required as a duty (बाध्यकारी)
• Involuntary: Done without conscious control (अनैच्छिक)
conceptTested: Knowledge of single words replacing descriptive phrases

subject: English
questionText:
In a digital era saturated with information, distinguishing fact from opinion has become increasingly difficult. News is often tailored to attract attention rather than inform, blurring the line between journalism and entertainment. This trend has significant implications for public opinion, as emotionally charged headlines can shape perceptions more than verified facts. Algorithms on social media further intensify this effect by filtering content based on prior user behavior, creating echo chambers. In such environments, individuals are more likely to encounter views they already agree with, reinforcing biases instead of challenging them. Media literacy, therefore, is essential. It involves the ability to critically evaluate sources, check for credibility, and recognize manipulative techniques. Without these skills, citizens risk forming views based on partial or misleading information. An informed public is not just a democratic ideal-it's a necessity in an age where truth can easily be distorted.

What is the primary concern the passage raises about modern news?

options.C: News often prioritizes attention over accuracy
options.c: News often prioritizes attention over accuracy

solution: The passage directly states: \"News is often tailored to attract attention rather than inform, blurring the line between journalism and entertainment.\" Thus, the author's primary concern is that news prioritizes attention over accuracy.
conceptTested: Reading comprehension and inference skills based on a given passage

subject: English
questionText:
Choose the correct indirect speech of the sentence:

She said, "I might consider your proposal."

options.A: She said she may consider my proposal.
options.B: She said she might considered my proposal.
options.C: She said she might consider my proposal.
options.D: She said she would considered my proposal.
options.a: She said she may consider my proposal.
options.b: She said she might considered my proposal.
options.c: She said she might consider my proposal.
options.d: She said she would considered my proposal.

solution: Rule: The modal auxiliary might remains unchanged in indirect speech, followed by the base form of the verb (V1: consider). The first - person pronoun 'I' changes to 'she', and 'your' changes to 'my'.
conceptTested: In indirect speech, past modal auxiliaries like might generally remain unchanged, and pronouns shift according to the speaker and listener.

questionText:
A sentence is provided in indirect speech. From the four given options, choose the one that most accurately conveys the sentence in its corresponding direct speech.

He said that no sooner had he arrived than the meeting began.

options.A: "No sooner I arrived than the meeting began, " he said.
options.B: "No sooner did I arrive than the meeting began, " he said.
options.C: "No sooner had I arrived than the meeting began, " he said.
options.D: "No sooner have I arrived than the meeting began, " he said.
options.a: "No sooner I arrived than the meeting began, " he said.
options.b: "No sooner did I arrive than the meeting began, " he said.
options.c: "No sooner had I arrived than the meeting began, " he said.
options.d: "No sooner have I arrived than the meeting began, " he said.

solution: Rule: The past perfect form with inverted syntax ("No sooner had + subject + V³ ... than ...") in indirect speech corresponds directly to the identical past perfect construction in direct speech with quotation marks and pronoun adjustment.
conceptTested: Direct speech using past perfect tense with inversion ("No sooner had...") corresponds directly to the same past perfect tense construction in indirect speech.
